overview: CS2102 completes the advanced-formation sim pair by focusing on separation and rejoin contracts: formation aborts, dissolving the flight, radial rendezvous, and fan-break recovery. The student should brief each procedure as a deconfliction problem first and a formation technique second.

studyNotes.headline: Discussion Items

items.text: An aborted takeoff in formation is first about maintaining aircraft control and preserving lateral separation.

children.text: Brief abort responsibilities before takeoff; do not let the first discussion happen after brake release.
If aborting, execute the NATOPS abort procedure, maintain directional control, stay on the assigned runway side, and transmit intentions when able.
If Lead aborts during an interval takeoff, Wing normally aborts behind Lead while maintaining Wing's runway side.
If Wing aborts during an interval takeoff, Wing aborts on Wing's side and transmits once Lead is safely airborne and Wing is under control.
If either aircraft aborts after section brake release, the aborting aircraft remains on its side and executes the abort.

The non-aborting aircraft recognizes the rapid line-of-sight rate, selects maximum power, maintains its runway side, and executes an individual takeoff unless separation cannot be maintained or it has its own emergency.
Wing must be ready to avoid Lead if Lead loses directional control, including changing runway sides or leaving the prepared surface if that is required to prevent collision.

items.text: Dissolving the flight turns a formation into individual aircraft while preserving positive separation, ATC coordination, and clear responsibility.

children.text: Complete required formation training and any needed lead change before the split.
Lead assigns heading and altitude separation; local event source uses at least 30 degrees of heading separation and normally 500 ft of altitude separation.
Wing normally turns away and descends to the assigned heading and altitude.
Lead maintains the original altitude until Wing reports established.
Use clear readbacks for heading, altitude, area, and detach clearance.
Wing sets the appropriate transponder or TCAS configuration per the brief and current local procedure.
Lead coordinates with ATC when the flight is splitting and dissolves the formation only after aircraft are established in their assigned blocks or areas.
For later rejoin, Wing reports ready on the tactical frequency and Lead coordinates the join clearance.
Keep local area names, frequencies, and route-specific calls tied to the day-of brief, not memorized as universal procedure.

items.text: Radial rendezvous is a structured blind or visual circular rendezvous that lets a separated flight rejoin using a known fix, altitude block, airspeed, and turn direction.

children.text: Lead establishes the rendezvous circle tangent to the briefed fix and flies the briefed direction.
Lead uses about 30 degrees AOB, maintains altitude and 200 KIAS, and calls position points at each 90-degree interval until Wing reports visual.
Lead adjusts for wind so point one remains tied to the fix.
Wing proceeds toward the point-one fix 500 ft below the briefed rendezvous altitude.
Wing remains 500 ft low until established on Lead's bearing line with fuselage alignment.
At point one, or another known circle point, Wing initiates the briefed turn direction even if Lead is not yet in sight.
Wing responds to Lead's position calls with DME or other briefed position awareness until visual.
After visual, Wing calls visual, climbs to Lead's altitude by placing Lead on the horizon, and completes the standard join-up.
If sight picture or situational awareness supports it, Wing may use the center of the circle as a control zone before beginning lead/lag maneuvering.
Do not rush from blind geometry into a high-closure join; preserve altitude separation until the visual rejoin is stable.

items.text: The fan break is a formation pattern-entry tool that creates interval through matched roll rate plus predictable power and speed-brake differences.

children.text: Lead initiates with the follow-me signal.
Lead smoothly rolls to about 45 degrees AOB at a rate Wing can match.
Lead normally holds power through about 90 degrees of turn, then retards the PCL to idle.
Lead makes required landing-pattern calls for the flight.
Wing matches Lead's roll rate.
Wing retards the PCL to idle and extends speed brake at maneuver start to build spacing.
Wing reports gear-down status after Lead's clearance-to-land call according to current SOP or course rules.
After landing, rejoin as a flight only after crossing the hold-short line and taxiing back together as briefed.
The maneuver depends on predictable timing; abrupt roll, late speed brake, or mismatched power can collapse spacing.
Use current local course rules for field-specific pattern calls and runway flow.

studyNotes.summary: CS2102 should be studied as a formation separation-and-rejoin event: abort safely, split the flight deliberately, rejoin with a structured radial rendezvous, and use fan-break spacing without improvising local calls.

summary: CS2102 covers formation aborts, flight split, radial rendezvous, and fan-break recovery.
title: Aborted Takeoff
